text: The masking pack of this story covers the 20 field IDs of v_ace_customer, DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074, and no field of the other 29 views; the clear identity number is out of reach in every case because the view returns id_no_masked (DF-ACE-073) and id_no_last4 (DF-ACE-074).
why: No source lists the personal field IDs the pack must cover, and the story has to write a bounded row set before it can build; leaving the set open would make the migration unreviewable.
read: Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074); TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.1 and the personal-data note; TSD P4 T3.1; FSD P4 A2.5
applied_in: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 to AC4; section 11 Data; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Build step 1
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer and the rwb-access tech lead when the pack design is published
impact: The wider field set adds rows to the same migration and to the same read; the answer rule, the boundary rule and the entry shape do not change.

text: The masking version of this story is MASK-2026.12, written on every row and named in every answer; the label is the one this Work Package fixes and not a source value.
why: A masking_rule row cannot be written and a masking answer cannot name its version without a label, and no source fixes one; the story must not invent a version format either.
read: TSD P4 T3.1 (masking_version varchar(20)); FSD P4 A2.4 and A2.5 (MASK-SIT-01 in an example); TSD P4 T3.2
applied_in: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background and AC2 to AC5 and AC9; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Business analyst, P4, and the rwb-access tech lead before the pack goes in force
impact: A different label changes the migration value and the expected answers only; no rule and no test step depends on the literal label.

text: A field is answered clear only where a masking_rule row for a role the caller holds, that field ID and the masking version in force says unmasked true; every other role is masked, including where no row exists, and no clear answer is ever derived from a permission letter.
why: The roster of unmasked roles is held by no source and the story cannot read one from the matrix; the only safe default is masked, which also matches the FSD rule that an uncovered personal field is masked.
read: FSD P4 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 T3.1 and T6.1; NFR-039; NFR-040
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC2 and AC3; section 8 BR2, BR6, BR7 and BR14; section 10 Authority
confirm: Security administrator and the Compliance and PDPA officer at the first pack load
impact: A published roster adds or removes unmasked rows in the pack and changes no code; the default stays masked.

text: The rwb-access database login keeps the service naming convention (schema rwb_access with one login) and is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' until the platform DB story fixes the name; this slice names no credential and adds no grant.
why: The legacy roles are the monolith's and the per-service login names are not fixed yet; the story must not invent a credential name or a grant.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41; DP-02; Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3; RWB-P1-E1069-DB
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC8; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: ACE team lead and the platform DB owner before the first migration runs
impact: Placeholder only; no behaviour depends on the literal name, and the privilege assertions stay as written.

text: masking_rule.field_id holds a dictionary field ID as a value in rwb_access, with no foreign key across schemas and no copy of a sys_fields or sys_objects row; the dictionary stays with rwb-source-data and rwb-access reads no P1 table.
why: The dictionary belongs to P1 and DP-01 forbids a cross-schema read, so the only reading that keeps the masking row in this service's schema is a value-keyed field ID.
read: Ownership Map (sys_fields and sys_objects to P1); Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P4 T3.1; DP-01
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Tables owned
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner at the data model review
impact: A dictionary API read would add a contract dependency and one hop to the masking read; the row shape and the answer do not change.

text: The module map of rwb-access holds no allowed source object, and boundary rule BND-6 refuses a class of the package that names a v_ace_* view as well as one that names a public table, failing the build with the class and the object named.
why: Only rwb-source-data reads the views, so this service's allow-list is empty by construction; the legacy rule refuses public tables only because its module map already held the 30 views as the allowed set.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-069 BR8, AC8 and section 13 (recovery-modules.yaml sourceViews); Architecture v5 slides 9 and 13; TSD P4 T1
applied_in: Section 5 X4 and X5; section 7 AC7; section 8 BR11; section 13 Components and Build step 6; section 14 Validation and messages
confirm: Tech lead, rwb-access, and the service template owner when the harness is published
impact: A published allow-list or a different wording changes the rule table and the message only; the build failure stays.
